purpose: Determine whether a small sideways pelvis velocity perturbation can produce single-foot support and enable backward initiation in repeated stalls.

design.dose_provenance: Within the 0.008 to 0.061 m/s range implied by pre-support displacement medians over the observed 140 ms interval.
design.physics: One bounded change in lateral root velocity relative to the body yaw. Prove no direct forward, vertical, joint, position or controller-history change. The two directions share the same captured physical state.
design.outcomes: Check lateral movement, first sustained single-foot support, original backward command speed and no loss or unsafe change on previously successful worlds.

installed_interface.coordinates: World-frame velocity at the body origin. Build a horizontal yaw-lateral vector from the measured root orientation and preserve vertical and angular entries.

preflight: Verify the installed simulator velocity setter and exact field scope at zero physics steps.
Independently verify matched state and two pure repeats, with fresh development seeds and original stall and action gates.
Freeze trigger and dose before new trajectories. Use only a pre-action stall marker and never the eventual contact side.
Treat any result as mechanism evidence. Require an actuator-compatible intervention and the original seven-command suite before promotion.
